title: Show that commuting staged544 moves cannot retarget a rank-1 ADD line
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Finite obstruction plus one scalar identity. No new κ. Selected conditional κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

On both pinned PR #3734 providers, every rank-1 ADD frame has a witness operand whose line is created by an entrance, a warp map, or an earlier rank-1 ADD that does not commute with it. Those witnesses are invariant under `apply_move`: non-map frames must contain their incoming state, and a warp cannot be relocated or crossed. After any finite sequence of commuting ADD moves, the frame still contains the original line. The crossed-line pattern left open by PR #3964 therefore does not occur on these words.

The same pattern, written as two scalar ADDs, keeps its opcodes, operands, and coefficients. Each of the two helpers contributes two rank-1 climbs before and after, so the child-histogram delta is zero. Either one-edit intermediate is illegal. An unchanged histogram is not a paid-profile gain.

Counts on each provider: 735 rank-1 ADDs, entrance 653, map 70, dependence 12. The twelve dependence pairs are adjacent read-after-write ADDs in section A.

This is not a supplier admission, not a noncommuting-rewrite theorem, and not a multiplication theorem. Frames that properly contain the old line, cleanup, native phases, owners, and all-size transfer are not repriced.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `scalar-to-moment`, scope **refined**. The card asks whether one scalar simplification changes a paid histogram. The object is the moved-ADD question released by PR #3964, on the two pinned providers and the `apply_move` contract, not a new R439 word.

  2. Single-hub two-bearing factorization of the PR #3573 certificate (comment 19021149).
  3. Bind one literal QQ16 six-tape event (comment 19030049).
  4. Integer-shear supplier/recurrence inequality left by #3947 (comments 19031016 and 19032401).

- Predecessor: open PR #3964, head `8a8bfb8d36cf5c9f7681b9e7f5d7876a4ba0f5a0`, proves the stationary case and leaves the moved-ADD question open. Its synthetic crossed-line control is not a provider occurrence.
- Parallel PR #4122 (discussion comment 19056694) prices a swap-and-restore identity at histogram delta zero and explicitly does not search the PR #3734 words. The added result here is the provider obstruction under `apply_move`. The two-ADD bill in this package recomputes the #3964 synthetic control; it is not a second claim on the #4122 invoice.
- Fork branch: https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/tree/cursor/staged544-moved-add-pair-00a3 at `b52f2efaff416cd1f464463e125e7ba4146c9c72`. Fork PR: https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/pull/18.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library, from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -B research/staged544-moved-add-pair/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/staged544-moved-add-pair
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/staged544-moved-add-pair --check-source-history
```

The direct verifier also passes under `python3.12 -O -B`. Observed marker:

```text
PASS_MOVED_ADD_PAIR providers=2 rank1=735 entrance=653 map=70 dependence=12 disjoint_line_moves=0 toy_helper_bill=4xrank1 toy_delta=0 no_new_kappa
```

`research_package.py` reports `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`. `check_research_commit.py` reports byte equality at the publication commit and source-history ancestry of `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f`.

Provider and tracer SHA-256 values are checked inside `verify.py`. The gzip words and `vendor/retiming.py` are unmodified copies from PR #3964. That commit is not an ancestor of this base, so `SOURCES.json` pins only the catalogue and the selected record.

The checker tests the witness partition and the window hypotheses. The invariance statement is a proof about every `apply_move` sequence, not an enumeration of those sequences. No Lean, Docker, or selected cold replay was run.

## Credit

The providers are dataisfire's PR #3734 words as vendored by Chris R / Clear1nsight in PR #3964. The stationary theorem, the crossed-line control, and `retiming.py` come from that PR and its credited PR #3886 / PR #3942 lineage. PR #4122 is the parallel abstract invoice. The witness partition and the invariance argument are new.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can one explicit noncommuting transposition, with a scalar correction, put a rank-1 ADD on a disjoint line and strictly lower the histogram for every real `0<a<1`? The twelve read-after-write pairs are the place to start. This obstruction stops at `crosses`, so that rewrite is a different identity. No such correction is specified here.
2. Does a commuting move whose new frame properly contains the old line improve the histogram? Containing frames are outside this theorem. PR #3970 already prices fixed-frame displacement two; a containing-frame census needs its own domain.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

Handoff-before-picker selection kept this off the randomized catalogue. A parallel session invoiced the abstract identity while this one was still on the provider trace; citing that PR in the package is what kept the two claims apart.
